findings.summary: Ardour is a cross-platform, open-source digital audio workstation designed for professional use. It provides a flexible routing system for mixing an unlimited number of tracks and buses, and supports sample-level editing operations such as trimming, splitting, and time-stretching. The software can function as a mastering environment and exports standard audio CD metadata. It integrates AI-assisted workflows through a Model Context Protocol server, allowing AI agents to manage plug-ins and MIDI data. Ardour adheres to industry standards for timing and format compatibility across Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and Windows.

mechanisms.title: Anything-to-anywhere routing and automation
mechanisms.explanation: Ardour uses an 'anything to anywhere' routing system that allows arbitrary connections between tracks and buses. Gain, panning, and plug-in parameters can be automated, and all internal mixing is performed in 32-bit floating-point format to maintain audio fidelity.

mechanisms.title: MCP server for AI-assisted workflows
mechanisms.explanation: Ardour supports AI-assisted workflows via a Model Context Protocol server. This mechanism allows AI agents to insert or remove audio plug-ins, create and edit MIDI notes and regions, and modify session information.
